chunk.text: Friends, now we have a top, top, top segment. You guys asked for this before, and you told us in the comment section that we should talk about this—something we also really wanted to discuss. Today, we don’t have both Divyansh with us, but we’ve still brought something special for you. Not just our own, but we’ll build it together. Yep. A La Liga vs Serie A all-time XI, friends. Wow! Welcome along. So, the plan was simple. This was supposed to happen three weeks ago. Yep. We had made a team yesterday, but now things have turned, and the plot is that we’ve submitted one of our all-time XIs. Okay, chat? And you guys will go along with us.

We will look at La Liga and Serie A all-time XIs one by one. Yep. Then we’ll have a debate among ourselves, and we’ll create a combined all-time XI together. Why did you put mine first? Oh! Oh man! It wasn’t like that—it was just a bit of a switch. Anyway, okay, okay. So, run us through this. Basically, for a La Liga and Serie A combined all-time XI, my goalkeeper was Iker Casillas. Of course, let’s start with the goalkeeper. Yes, let’s go. This is your team—let’s do it one by one. Should I explain my team or wait? No, talk about the goalkeeper first.

I think I’ll go with Casillas because, personally, the phase in which he joined Real Madrid—Madrid has always been a top club—but there was a big transition. He was a very young goalkeeper at a top club, and after that, he became number one. For Spain, he won the Euros and the World Cup—Euros twice, as captain. I think he is one of the most decorated goalkeepers you could see. Very tough choice, but I would go with Casillas. Bro, let’s show the other teams one by one so the audience can see them. I’ll also mention what other goalkeepers were picked.

So, Yash has taken Iker Casillas as his goalkeeper in the all-time XI, but I think the other four have gone for Buffon. Wow, really? Yes, all four of us have gone for Buffon. I want you to explain—why Buffon over Casillas? Because Casillas came into an already strong Real Madrid team and was somewhat set up to succeed. But when we talk about Buffon, he came from Parma, and then Juventus got relegated, yet he stayed with them.

He did. And he won the World Cup with Italy. After that, he won so many titles with Juventus and reached Champions League finals as well, although he couldn’t win one. But if we talk about longevity, he was playing top-tier football till the age of 40. We can’t say the same about Casillas. Yes, he peaked beautifully, but I think Buffon has the edge. Chat, who would you take—Buffon or Casillas? I chose Buffon. My reasoning was simple: for this all-time XI, I focused mainly on club careers and did not consider international achievements.

And this is where things get interesting. When we talk about Buffon, he is one of the longest-serving goalkeepers in football. He has won multiple Serie A titles—if I’m not wrong, around 11. He is among the most decorated players in Serie A history. Of course, Juventus were dominant, similar to Bayern Munich in Germany, winning multiple league titles in a row.

Juventus had that dominance, just like Bayern. Meanwhile, Real Madrid had more competition in La Liga because of Barcelona. So, winning the league was tougher. However, in the Champions League, Madrid had a period where they struggled, often getting knocked out in the round of 16 or quarterfinals between 2004 and 2010. That weakens Casillas’ case slightly.

So, the case for Casillas is weaker in that period. Even league-wise, the titles weren’t as many. Meanwhile, Buffon had consistency and longevity. He started at Parma and maintained top-level performance for years. The chat is also mostly supporting Buffon. Another key point is that when Juventus were relegated to Serie B, Buffon stayed with them, which says a lot about his loyalty and character.

Physically, Buffon also seemed like a more commanding presence—taller and more dominant. I think we all agree that Buffon will be our combined goalkeeper. The majority has chosen him. So, Buffon it is. Now, let’s move to the centre-back partnership and look at the backline.

We have Sergio Ramos, Paolo Maldini, and some have chosen Baresi. Others have gone with Cafu at right-back. That’s a strong pick. In my team, I had Maldini, Baresi, and Ramos, with Dani Alves at right-back. Some others picked Zanetti, which is also a great choice.

I wanted to include a slightly different player because there are so many great Italian defenders. Nesta was another option. Zanetti also deserves recognition for his longevity and consistency. Overall, we all seem to agree on Maldini and Baresi in the backline.

So, we are going with a back four. Maldini, Baresi, and Sergio Ramos are almost certain picks. Maldini, although often remembered as a centre-back, originally played as a left-back. Baresi was also incredibly successful, winning major trophies including the Champions League.

For right-back, I went with Dani Alves. Initially, I considered Zanetti and Cafu, but when I looked deeper into Dani Alves’ career, it was clear he belongs at the top. His achievements and consistency are incredible.

I was discussing this recently—why isn’t Dani Alves rated as highly as he should be? When comparing him with Cafu and Zanetti, people often focus on international success. But in terms of club football, Dani Alves has been phenomenal.
Zanetti, for example, peaked later in his career and had great longevity, but Dani Alves played for top clubs and consistently delivered. He is one of the most decorated players in football history.

Since 2005, with the introduction of FIFPro World XI selections, Dani Alves has consistently featured among the best. He has performed at the highest level with multiple clubs and has over 150 assists as a fullback, which is incredible.
That’s true. But when I was making my team, I wasn’t only looking at trophies. Cafu revolutionized the right-back role—overlapping runs, attacking play—he defined that position in many ways.

The reason I picked Roberto Carlos is that he revolutionized the left-back role. He was more than just a defender—he was an attacking force, a set-piece specialist, and one of the most exciting players to watch.
And when it comes to centre-backs, Sergio Ramos stands out for his performances in big moments. He was a leader, a winner, and someone who consistently delivered when it mattered most.
Roberto Carlos, on the other hand, changed how we view left-backs. He had incredible attacking ability, scored goals, and was one of the best set-piece takers in football history.
Serie A defenders faced some of the best attackers in the world week in and week out—players like Maradona, Ronaldo, and others. That makes their achievements even more impressive.
So, we all agree on a back four: Maldini at left-back, Baresi and Ramos as centre-backs, and Dani Alves at right-back.
Now we move to the midfield. This is where it gets really interesting because there are so many great players to choose from.

text: We also did not take Inzaghi. We have left him out. But Inzaghi was more of a super-sub.
